results.name: Stray Cat, Open Doors: How k0t Wanders Through the Network Edge
results.description: Group-IB and NyxLab uncovered a large-scale campaign by threat actor k0t exploiting FortiGate, FortiWeb, and Palo Alto GlobalProtect edge devices to harvest credentials and establish persistent access. The operation involves exploiting CVE-2025-64446 in FortiWeb and CVE-2026-0257 in GlobalProtect, alongside brute-forcing attacks using custom tools. Over 70,000 exposed credentials were discovered, with victims spanning multiple industries globally. Post-compromise activities include credential theft, Active Directory enumeration, and data exfiltration via Rclone to cloud storage. Persistence is maintained through MeshCentral, AdaptixC2, and various RMM tools including Atera and AnyDesk. The campaign shows overlaps with Qilin and The Gentlemen ransomware groups, suggesting k0t may operate as an Initial Access Broker, though direct affiliation remains unconfirmed.

results.name: "Next Exploit Opportunities": How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities
results.description: A financially motivated threat actor operating under the handle BUGSTER leveraged jailbroken AI assistants, specifically the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4, to conduct multiple cybercrime operations across India. The actor, demonstrating limited technical skills but relying heavily on AI-generated scripts and reconnaissance, successfully exfiltrated over 5,200 personal records from a university database, conducted WordPress brute force attacks, and planned VoIP telecommunications fraud. Additional activities included Wi-Fi password cracking requiring physical proximity to targets, cryptocurrency whale reconnaissance, and development of credential scanning toolkits. The actor configured specialized AI bot profiles providing step-by-step criminal guidance, including fraud traffic ratios and carrier evasion techniques, demonstrating how AI lowers the skill barrier for cybercrime operations.

results.name: Amazon-Themed ClickFix Campaign Serves Up Finger-Licking Malware
results.description: Attackers leveraged a sponsored Google search result for 'amazon business' to redirect victims to a spoofed Amazon login page hosted on Google Sites. The page presented a fake CAPTCHA (ClickFix) that tricked users into executing a malicious command using Windows' finger utility, an obsolete network tool repurposed as a living-off-the-land binary. This initiated a complex infection chain downloading IronPython, executing obfuscated Python scripts, and deploying multiple payloads including Doina malware, Lumma Stealer via a Node.js package, and a pirated NetSupport Client RMM tool. The attack infrastructure predominantly used barbecue-themed domains for command and control. The campaign affected multiple organizations and demonstrates cross-platform capabilities, with alternate payloads prepared for macOS users. Attackers employed sophisticated obfuscation techniques including Base64 encoding with Cyrillic character substitution, XOR encryption, and RC4 decryption throughout the infection stages.

results.name: Uncovered and Disrupted BADBOX 3.0, the Largest Ad Fraud Operation by Bid Volume Ever Publicly Disclosed
results.description: BADBOX 3.0 represents the largest ad fraud operation ever disclosed, generating approximately 40 billion bid requests daily and comprising over 4% of all connected TV traffic. The operation primarily targets low-cost consumer devices infected with backdoors delivering fraud modules linked to TXCZ, a Chinese electronics manufacturer. These modules render invisible video ads while impersonating legitimate applications and enroll devices as exit nodes in eleven residential proxy networks, including PXYEDGE, the successor to IpMoYu from BADBOX 2.0. The operation also employs spoofed server-side ad insertion traffic. The campaign's volume exceeds the previous record holder VASTFLUX by three times and surpasses the combined volume of five years of prior investigations.

results.name: Device Code Phishing in Microsoft 365: Attack Analysis
results.description: In November 2026, a resurgence of device-code phishing campaigns targeted Microsoft 365 accounts using payment-themed emails and fake SharePoint workspaces. Attackers delivered obfuscated HTML and SVG attachments that redirected victims through verification gates to counterfeit document-sharing pages. These lures instructed recipients to enter attacker-supplied codes into genuine Microsoft authorization pages, exploiting the device-code authentication flow. When victims completed authentication, including MFA, attacker-controlled clients received access tokens with granted permissions. The campaigns employed sophisticated obfuscation techniques including fragment reversal, Base64 substitution, and XOR encoding. Session-status checks and heartbeat mechanisms coordinated the phishing pages with backend infrastructure. The attacks combined legitimate business correspondence pretexts with Microsoft's authentic sign-in infrastructure to deceive users into authorizing malicious access requests.

results.name: UAT-12643: Suspected North Korea-aligned actor blends blockchain resilience with targeted infostealing
results.description: A financially motivated threat group designated UAT-12643 has been discovered operating malicious infrastructure targeting cryptocurrency holders, gaming platform users, and VoIP software operators. The actor deploys multiple payloads including the Overlord RAT, Python-based Good Game infostealer, and a multi-cryptocurrency clipboard hijacker. The Overlord RAT employs an innovative command-and-control resilience technique by embedding encrypted server URLs in Solana blockchain transaction memos. Potential victims are located primarily in Europe based on file harvesting capabilities targeting English, French, Spanish, and Portuguese documents. The campaign demonstrates overlaps with known North Korean APT tactics, particularly through the use of Overlord RAT and Solana blockchain techniques previously attributed to Lazarus Group and UNK_DeadDrop cluster. Lure themes suggest targeting of finance staff, VoIP operators, and cryptocurrency users across multiple sectors.

results.name: N0N Ransomware Group: Victims, Leak Site, TTPs & IOCs
results.description: N0N is a financially motivated cyber extortion group that emerged in September 2026, employing data theft and extortion tactics without using traditional encryption methods. The group leverages compromised credentials obtained from third-party infostealer campaigns to infiltrate corporate networks. Once inside, they exfiltrate sensitive information including Active Directory mappings and legal documents, then threaten public disclosure via dark web leak sites to coerce ransom payments. N0N targets multiple sectors including investment services, telecommunications, retail, education, and pharmaceuticals across 54 countries. Their approach avoids conventional file encryption, instead manipulating victim data through administrative tools, making detection more challenging for traditional security controls.

results.name: Inside the 'Party' Panel: How Fraudsters Rent Android Banking Trojans to Target Indian Bank Customers
results.description: A multi-tenant malware-as-a-service platform enables fraudsters to deploy fake Google Play pages and branded Android banking trojans targeting Indian financial institutions. The operation, discovered via an unprotected server, hosted 50 tenant accounts with 34 active paid licenses targeting customers of six Indian banks and card issuers. Victims are lured through convincing fake Play Store pages that harvest card details, CVV, and personal information before delivering a two-stage malware. The dropper bypasses Android 13+ security by impersonating the Play Store installation process, while the hidden payload steals SMS-based OTPs, uploads sensitive photos, and redirects phone calls using call-forwarding codes. The infrastructure leverages Firebase and Telegram for command-and-control, with all indicators pointing to an India-based operator exploiting Indian hosting providers and targeting domestic financial customers and government service users.

results.name: Unsolicited audits: how AuditTeam masks ransomware
results.description: AuditTeam is an active threat group operating since January 2026, using the sophisticated OpsAgent framework to compromise organizations across multiple countries including Russia, Italy, Philippines, Hong Kong, Senegal, Finland, and China. The group demands an 'Audit & Consulting fee' for vulnerability reports, masking ransomware operations as security consulting. OpsAgent evolved from C++ to Rust implementation, providing extensive capabilities including file system management, process injection, privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture, and network pivoting. The framework uses AWS CloudFront subdomains for command-and-control, discovered via GitHub repositories. Two specialized modules extend functionality: an AV/EDR killer using a signed Beijing Jiangmin Antivirus driver to terminate security products, and a cryptor module encrypting files with AES-CBC or ChaCha20 while targeting database processes. results.name: Attackers Exploit Optimizely Flaw To Inject Malicious JavaScript
results.description: On November 16, 2026, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation account signup flow, allowing unauthorized modification of the Project JavaScript field. This enabled injection of malicious JavaScript into customer projects, which was then delivered to website visitors through legitimate Optimizely snippets served from their CDN. The malicious payload was designed to replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Litecoin, Toncoin, Bitcoin Cash, and Dogecoin. It also performed payment card skimming, cookie theft, screen capture functionality, and delivered iOS exploit kits (Coruna and DarkSword) targeting iPhones and iPads. ThreatLabz identified over 450 unique domains and 3,000 URLs serving the malicious script, affecting multiple industries including airlines, automotive, banking, e-commerce, insurance, media, real estate, retail, telecommunications, and technology sectors.
